emergency.note: 911 is the unified emergency number in Makkah Province; legacy numbers 999 (police), 997 (ambulance) and 998 (civil defence) also work, and English-speaking operators are common in pilgrimage seasons.

hood_desc: A large modern district southeast of the Haram packed with hotels, apartments and restaurants popular with pilgrims; suits Umrah and Hajj visitors wanting mid-range value with shuttle or taxi access to the Grand Mosque.
A central district immediately south of the Masjid al-Haram, wall-to-wall pilgrim hotels within walking distance of the Kaaba; suits pilgrims who want to be steps from prayers, at premium prices.
A dense central quarter southwest of the Haram with budget and mid-range hotels within walking reach; suits pilgrims wanting closeness to the mosque without top-tier prices.
A historic area right beside the Grand Mosque near the Clock Tower complex, redeveloped with hotels; suits pilgrims wanting maximum proximity and modern lodging by the Haram.
A residential district on the outskirts along the Makkah-Jeddah road with cheaper lodging farther from the Haram; suits budget pilgrims and those with transport who do not mind commuting to prayers.

water.note: Treated water meets standards, but bottled water is commonly preferred due to plumbing and taste.

transit.pay: Book Haramain train tickets online or via the HHR app/station counters (Mecca-Jeddah-Medina, roughly SAR 90-300 / $24-80 depending on class); city buses take cash in Saudi riyals for a few riyals a ride. The Al Mashaaer Metro is free but restricted to pilgrims with Hajj permits during the Hajj season only.
transit.hours: Haramain trains run multiple daily departures roughly 6am-midnight; city buses operate through the day with extended hours during Hajj and Ramadan; the Al Mashaaer Metro runs only a few days a year during Hajj.
transit.note: Public transit here is built around pilgrim logistics rather than general tourism; most visitors combine buses and the Haramain train with organized group transport.

transit.m: Haramain High Speed Train to Makkah station, ~55 min

landmarks: Masjid al-Haram (Great Mosque of Mecca)
Islam's holiest mosque, surrounding the Kaaba, its vast illuminated courtyard is one of the most photographed religious sites on Earth.
The Kaaba
The cubic structure at the center of Islam's holiest site, draped in black kiswah cloth, toward which Muslims worldwide pray.
Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower
A soaring clock tower complex overlooking the Grand Mosque, offering a dramatic modern skyline backdrop at night.
Jabal al-Nour (Mountain of Light)
A striking desert peak on Mecca's edge, notable as the city's highest point and a scenic vantage over the surrounding valley.
Cave of Hira
A small cave near the summit of Jabal al-Nour, traditionally revered as the site of Islam's first revelation.
Mount Arafat (Jabal al-Rahmah)
A granite hill east of Mecca central to the Hajj, memorable for the sight of vast crowds of pilgrims gathered on its slopes.
Zamzam Well
A historic sacred well beneath the Grand Mosque, long central to Mecca's pilgrimage traditions.
Mina Tent City
A vast valley of white fireproof tents that becomes a striking sea of uniform structures during the Hajj season.
Safa and Marwa
Two small hills enclosed within the Grand Mosque where pilgrims perform the ritual walk of Sa'i, now a striking marble-lined gallery.
Mecca City Skyline at Night
The view of central Mecca illuminated after dark, with the Grand Mosque and clock tower glowing against the surrounding mountains.

train.note: Mecca (Makkah) is on the Haramain High-Speed Railway, with fast domestic trains linking it to Jeddah (city centre and airport/KAEC) and Madinah at up to 300 km/h. No international trains.

bus.note: Note that non-Muslims may not enter Mecca. SAPTCO runs domestic coaches across the Kingdom and international services to Gulf/Arab countries; foreign pilgrims usually connect via Jeddah. Carry your passport and visa for any cross-border trip.

ferry.note: Mecca is inland with no ferries. The nearest port is Jeddah (about 85 km) on the Red Sea, which has at times operated seasonal Hajj/Umrah pilgrim ferries across to Egypt and Sudan - confirm current sailings before relying on them.
